name: castor
description: Point it at any web page and it finds the video, transcodes it, and streams it to your TV in real time. It even burns in subtitles.
readmeExcerpt:
# Castor Cast web video to your TV without screen mirroring. Castor finds streams, converts incompatible formats, and optionally generates subtitles. Run locally or offload media processing to a NAS. No bundled content or sources; DRM streams are refused. Use content you are authorized to access.

## Quick start Install with one of (requirements in [Installation](#installation)): ```sh # macOS brew install --cask stupside/tap/castor # Any platform, Node 20+ npm install -g @castor-dev/cli # From source, Go 1.27+ and cmake git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/stupside/castor.git && cd castor && make build ``` Then discover your devices: ```sh castor scan ``` Save `config.yaml` in your working directory using the name and type from the scan: ```yaml device: name: "Living Room TV" type: dlna # dlna, chromecast, or roku ``` Then cast a page or a direct video URL: ```sh castor cast player https://example.com/watch/some-video castor cast url https://example.com/video.m3u8 ``` If discovery finds nothing, see [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting). ## Installation Whichever way you install, you also need Chrome/Chromium for webpage extraction and **ffmpeg + ffprobe 7.1+** for media processing, on `PATH`. Encoding uses a working GPU encoder when available, with software fallback. On Windows: `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg` and `winget install Google.Chrome`, and allow Castor on private networks. No Homebrew or Node? Extract the [latest release](https://github.com/stupside/castor/releases/latest) for your platform (`.tar.gz` for Linux, `.zip` for Windows) and put `castor` or `castor.exe` on `PATH`. ## Commands | Command | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `castor scan` | Discover devices | | `castor cast player ` | Cast a webpage's video | | `castor cast url ` | Cast a direct stream or video | | `castor cast` | Browse titles interactively; requires a TMDB key and sources | | `castor cast movie ` | Cast a movie using your source templates | | `castor cast episode --season N --episode N` | Cast an episode using your source templates | Add `--dry-run` to a cast command to list resolved streams without casting, and `--at 1h12m` (or `1:12`) to begin at a position; `castor cast` asks for one after you pick a title. Once playing, a DLNA device's own seek works when castor serves it one MPEG-TS stream of a source with a declared duration and no generated captions: castor reads the source again from the position asked for. Use `castor --help` for all flags and `--debug` for diagnostics. ## Configuration Castor loads `config.yaml` (or `--config `), overlays git-ignored `config.local.yaml`, then applies environment overrides such as `CASTOR_CAST__MAX_HEIGHT=720`. Keep secrets in the local file or environment. See the annotated [config.yaml](config.yaml) for service settings and the [migration guide](migrations/1.x-to-2.0.md) when upgrading from 1.x. ### Playback preferences ```yaml cast: max_height: 1080 # select within this ceiling; scale taller video max_bitrate: 6M # ask no more of the device's link; a heavier picture, and sound, are re-encoded under it audio: languages: [fr, en] # ordered preferences; otherwise source default subtitles: languages: [fr, en] # ordered source caption preferences transcribe_if_missing: false # opt in to Whisper-generated captions delivery: auto # serve forces playback through Castor ``` Source captions are supported on Chromecast and DLNA. Without usable captions, playback continues without subtitles unless transcription is enabled. Generated captions use a native track where supported, otherwise they are burned into video. Whisper downloads its default model once; set `servers.media.whisper.model_path` for a custom model. English-only models require English. ### Title browsing and sources Interactive browsing needs a [TMDB key](https://www.themoviedb.org/settings/api). Title commands need templates for sites you are authorized to use; proxies are tried in order: ```yaml tmdb: api_key: "" sources: - proxies: ["https://your-source.example"] templates: movie: "/embed/movie/{itemID}" episode: "/embed/tv/{itemID}/{season}-{episode}" ``` ## Supported devices | Protocol | Support | | --- | --- | | DLNA / UPnP (`MediaRenderer:1`) | Smart TVs and compatible players; tested on Samsung | | Chromecast | Experimental; not yet tested on real hardware | | Roku | Experimental; requires a playback channel; not yet tested on real hardware | ### Roku setup 1. Enable Developer Mode: press **Home ×3, Up ×2, Right, Left, Right, Left, Right**, then enable it and set a web-server password. The device reboots. 2. Set `servers.api.devices.roku.password` in `config.local.yaml`. 3. Castor sideloads its channel on the first cast and reuses it afterward. For a published channel, set `servers.api.devices.roku.app_id` instead. Relayed Roku playback runs about 30 seconds behind. ## Remote services By default, CLI commands embed missing services. To offload processing, run `castor media-server` on your NAS with `servers.media.token` set. On your computer: ```yaml servers: media: url: http://my-nas:8410 token: "" ``` Your computer controls the TV; the NAS processes and serves media. Set `servers.media.advertise` on the server if its chosen address is unreachable from the TV. For apps or a shared API, run each service separately: | Command | Default port | Runs where | | --- | --- | --- | | `castor media-server` | 8410 | Devices can fetch its media URLs | | `castor scraping-server` | 8412 | Chrome is installed | | `castor api-server` | 8411 | It can discover and control devices | Configure API with `servers.media.url`, `servers.scraping.url`, and their tokens. Give each service its own token; clients use `servers.api.url` and `servers.api.token`. Standalone servers listen on all interfaces by default. Use HTTPS outside a trusted network; see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). The API exposes device listing, cast/stop, and status watching through [Connect contracts](proto/castor/v1). For example, list devices: ```sh curl -X POST http://localhost:8411/castor.v1.DeviceService/ListDevices \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' ``` See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for service ownership and cast lifecycle. ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Check | | --- | --- | | No devices discovered | Discovery normally stays on one subnet. Set `device.host` to the TV's IP to skip it; for DLNA, a description URL also works. Required on Android/Termux. | | Devices share a name | Set `device.id` to the ID printed by `castor scan`. | | Page video is not found | The video must start without a click; DRM streams are refused. | | TV loads but cannot play | Try `CASTOR_CAST__DELIVERY=serve castor --debug cast url ` to force served playback. | | TV cannot fetch served media | Allow Castor through the firewall and check `servers.media.advertise` and `servers.media.network.interface`. Leave the interface unset on Android/Termux. | Devices fetch media and captions on **8410** for a standalone media server, or a random LAN port for an embedded one. Discovery uses SSDP UDP 1900 (DLNA/Roku) and mDNS UDP 5353 (Chromecast). Outbound control uses Chromecast TCP 8009, Roku TCP 8060 (80 for sideloading), or DLNA's advertised port. API and scraping ports are for service clients. Logs include a shared `cast_id` across services. With remote services, inspect each server's logs. Set `telemetry.endpoint` to an OTLP/HTTP collector's base URL to export logs, traces and metrics (castor adds `/v1/logs`, `/v1/traces` and `/v1/metrics`). Every service needs it, and trace context follows a cast across them. Exported records carry `castor.cast.id`, and castor's own names sit under `castor.`. ```sh docker run --rm -p 3000:3000 -p 4318:4318 \ -v "$PWD/docker/grafana:/otel-lgtm/grafana/conf/provisioning/dashboards:ro" \ grafana/otel-lgtm # Grafana on :3000 (admin/admin) with the Castor dashboard CASTOR_TELEMETRY__ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318 castor cast ``` ## Docker The image includes Chrome, ffmpeg and ffprobe. Use **Linux host networking** for discovery and device-reachable media URLs; native binaries are simpler for discovery on macOS/Windows. ```sh docker run --rm --network host \ -v "$PWD/config.yaml:/config.yaml:ro" \ -v castor-cache:/root/.cache \ ghcr.io/stupside/castor:latest \ cast player https://example.com/watch/some-video ``` Add `--device /dev/dri` for Intel VA-API; otherwise encoding uses software. The cache volume preserves Whisper models. For the [Compose stack](docker-compose.yml), put `CASTOR_SERVERS__MEDIA__TOKEN`, `CASTOR_SERVERS__SCRAPING__TOKEN`, and `CASTOR_SERVERS__API__TOKEN` in git-ignored `.env`, then run `docker compose up -d`. Remove the `/dev/dri` mapping on hosts without that device. A bridged media container needs `-p 8410:8410` and a device-reachable `servers.media.advertise`. Image tags: `latest` (stable), `canary` (preview), or a pinned `vX.Y.Z`. ## Contributing and purpose See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) to build or contribute. Castor provides no content, sources, or DRM circumvention. You are responsible for lawful use and compliance with site terms. Provided as-is for lawful, personal and educational use.
readmeHtml:
Castor

Cast web video to your TV without screen mirroring. Castor finds streams, converts incompatible formats, and optionally generates subtitles. Run locally or offload media processing to a NAS.

No bundled content or sources; DRM streams are refused. Use content you are authorized to access.

Quick start

Install with one of (requirements in Installation):

# macOS
brew install --cask stupside/tap/castor

# Any platform, Node 20+
npm install -g @castor-dev/cli

# From source, Go 1.27+ and cmake
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/stupside/castor.git && cd castor && make build

Then discover your devices:

castor scan

Save config.yaml in your working directory using the name and type from the scan:

device:
  name: "Living Room TV"
  type: dlna               # dlna, chromecast, or roku

Then cast a page or a direct video URL:

castor cast player https://example.com/watch/some-video
castor cast url https://example.com/video.m3u8

If discovery finds nothing, see Troubleshooting.

Installation

Whichever way you install, you also need Chrome/Chromium for webpage extraction and ffmpeg + ffprobe 7.1+ for media processing, on PATH. Encoding uses a working GPU encoder when available, with software fallback.

On Windows: winget install Gyan.FFmpeg and winget install Google.Chrome, and allow Castor on private networks.

No Homebrew or Node? Extract the latest release for your platform (.tar.gz for Linux, .zip for Windows) and put castor or castor.exe on PATH.

Commands

Command Purpose
castor scan Discover devices
castor cast player <url> Cast a webpage's video
castor cast url <url> Cast a direct stream or video
castor cast Browse titles interactively; requires a TMDB key and sources
castor cast movie <id> Cast a movie using your source templates
castor cast episode <id> --season N --episode N Cast an episode using your source templates

Add --dry-run to a cast command to list resolved streams without casting, and --at 1h12m (or 1:12) to begin at a position; castor cast asks for one after you pick a title. Once playing, a DLNA device's own seek works when castor serves it one MPEG-TS stream of a source with a declared duration and no generated captions: castor reads the source again from the position asked for. Use castor --help for all flags and --debug for diagnostics.

Configuration

Castor loads config.yaml (or --config <path>), overlays git-ignored config.local.yaml, then applies environment overrides such as CASTOR_CAST__MAX_HEIGHT=720. Keep secrets in the local file or environment. See the annotated config.yaml for service settings and the migration guide when upgrading from 1.x.

Playback preferences

cast:
  max_height: 1080          # select within this ceiling; scale taller video
  max_bitrate: 6M           # ask no more of the device's link; a heavier picture, and sound, are re-encoded under it
  audio:
    languages: [fr, en]    # ordered preferences; otherwise source default
  subtitles:
    languages: [fr, en]    # ordered source caption preferences
    transcribe_if_missing: false  # opt in to Whisper-generated captions
  delivery: auto           # serve forces playback through Castor

Source captions are supported on Chromecast and DLNA. Without usable captions, playback continues without subtitles unless transcription is enabled. Generated captions use a native track where supported, otherwise they are burned into video. Whisper downloads its default model once; set servers.media.whisper.model_path for a custom model. English-only models require English.

Title browsing and sources

Interactive browsing needs a TMDB key. Title commands need templates for sites you are authorized to use; proxies are tried in order:

tmdb:
  api_key: "<KEY>"
sources:
  - proxies: ["https://your-source.example"]
    templates:
      movie: "/embed/movie/{itemID}"
      episode: "/embed/tv/{itemID}/{season}-{episode}"

Supported devices

Protocol Support
DLNA / UPnP (MediaRenderer:1) Smart TVs and compatible players; tested on Samsung
Chromecast Experimental; not yet tested on real hardware
Roku Experimental; requires a playback channel; not yet tested on real hardware

Roku setup

  1. Enable Developer Mode: press Home ×3, Up ×2, Right, Left, Right, Left, Right, then enable it and set a web-server password. The device reboots.
  2. Set servers.api.devices.roku.password in config.local.yaml.
  3. Castor sideloads its channel on the first cast and reuses it afterward.

For a published channel, set servers.api.devices.roku.app_id instead. Relayed Roku playback runs about 30 seconds behind.

Remote services

By default, CLI commands embed missing services. To offload processing, run castor media-server on your NAS with servers.media.token set. On your computer:

servers:
  media:
    url: http://my-nas:8410
    token: "<same token as the server>"

Your computer controls the TV; the NAS processes and serves media. Set servers.media.advertise on the server if its chosen address is unreachable from the TV.

For apps or a shared API, run each service separately:

Command Default port Runs where
castor media-server 8410 Devices can fetch its media URLs
castor scraping-server 8412 Chrome is installed
castor api-server 8411 It can discover and control devices

Configure API with servers.media.url, servers.scraping.url, and their tokens. Give each service its own token; clients use servers.api.url and servers.api.token. Standalone servers listen on all interfaces by default. Use HTTPS outside a trusted network; see SECURITY.md.

The API exposes device listing, cast/stop, and status watching through Connect contracts. For example, list devices:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8411/castor.v1.DeviceService/ListDevices \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'

See ARCHITECTURE.md for service ownership and cast lifecycle.

Troubleshooting

Symptom Check
No devices discovered Discovery normally stays on one subnet. Set device.host to the TV's IP to skip it; for DLNA, a description URL also works. Required on Android/Termux.
Devices share a name Set device.id to the ID printed by castor scan.
Page video is not found The video must start without a click; DRM streams are refused.
TV loads but cannot play Try CASTOR_CAST__DELIVERY=serve castor --debug cast url <url> to force served playback.
TV cannot fetch served media Allow Castor through the firewall and check servers.media.advertise and servers.media.network.interface. Leave the interface unset on Android/Termux.

Devices fetch media and captions on 8410 for a standalone media server, or a random LAN port for an embedded one. Discovery uses SSDP UDP 1900 (DLNA/Roku) and mDNS UDP 5353 (Chromecast). Outbound control uses Chromecast TCP 8009, Roku TCP 8060 (80 for sideloading), or DLNA's advertised port. API and scraping ports are for service clients.

Logs include a shared cast_id across services. With remote services, inspect each server's logs.

Set telemetry.endpoint to an OTLP/HTTP collector's base URL to export logs, traces and metrics (castor adds /v1/logs, /v1/traces and /v1/metrics). Every service needs it, and trace context follows a cast across them. Exported records carry castor.cast.id, and castor's own names sit under castor..

docker run --rm -p 3000:3000 -p 4318:4318 \
  -v "$PWD/docker/grafana:/otel-lgtm/grafana/conf/provisioning/dashboards:ro" \
  grafana/otel-lgtm   # Grafana on :3000 (admin/admin) with the Castor dashboard
CASTOR_TELEMETRY__ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318 castor cast

Docker

The image includes Chrome, ffmpeg and ffprobe. Use Linux host networking for discovery and device-reachable media URLs; native binaries are simpler for discovery on macOS/Windows.

docker run --rm --network host \
  -v "$PWD/config.yaml:/config.yaml:ro" \
  -v castor-cache:/root/.cache \
  ghcr.io/stupside/castor:latest \
  cast player https://example.com/watch/some-video

Add --device /dev/dri for Intel VA-API; otherwise encoding uses software. The cache volume preserves Whisper models.

For the Compose stack, put CASTOR_SERVERS__MEDIA__TOKEN, CASTOR_SERVERS__SCRAPING__TOKEN, and CASTOR_SERVERS__API__TOKEN in git-ignored .env, then run docker compose up -d. Remove the /dev/dri mapping on hosts without that device. A bridged media container needs -p 8410:8410 and a device-reachable servers.media.advertise.

Image tags: latest (stable), canary (preview), or a pinned vX.Y.Z.

Contributing and purpose

See CONTRIBUTING.md to build or contribute. Castor provides no content, sources, or DRM circumvention. You are responsible for lawful use and compliance with site terms. Provided as-is for lawful, personal and educational use.

* Castor 1.x configuration must be migrated to the cast and servers sections. See the [1.x → 2.0 migration guide](https://github.com/stupside/castor/blob/main/migrations/1.x-to-2.0.md).

* **api:** log the address of the device a client lends, which the contract sends for that ([4205f3e](https://github.com/stupside/castor/commit/4205f3ee2c20d0838bcb6d2638a673ce91d09537))

discussions.title: Let's improve Castor: What device do you cast to ?

aiSummary.oneLiner: A CLI tool for extracting and streaming high-quality web video directly to Chromecast and DLNA devices
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Castor is a command-line utility that allows users to cast web videos to smart TVs at their native quality, bypassing the resolution drops and latency typical of screen mirroring. When pointed at a web page or direct stream URL, Castor launches a headless Chrome instance, monitors network traffic via the Chrome DevTools Protocol to intercept the actual video stream, and then transcodes or streams it directly to the local casting device. It includes a fallback interaction pipeline to simulate user clicks on iframes to trigger playback on stubborn sites. It also supports resolving media IDs against custom sources and burning in auto-generated subtitles.
keyFeatures: Stream interception: uses a headless browser and the Chrome DevTools Protocol to intercept raw video streams from complex web players.
Native casting: sends the extracted video directly to the TV for full-resolution playback rather than relying on lossy screen mirroring.
Automated interaction: runs a pipeline to automatically click through iframes and play buttons to extract streams from recalcitrant websites.
Live transcoding: utilizes FFmpeg to convert incompatible video streams into formats supported by the target casting device on the fly.
Subtitle burn-in: automatically generates and burns subtitles directly into the video stream before casting.
Terminal user interface: provides an interactive CLI for browsing media, selecting casting devices, and managing playback.

useCases.title: High-Quality Web Casting
useCases.description: Allows users to cast embedded videos from non-standard websites to their smart TV without resorting to laggy screen mirroring.

useCases.title: IPTV Stream Bridging
useCases.description: Enables users to extract direct IPTV streams from obscure web portals and send them reliably to a Chromecast.

useCases.title: Automated Media Resolution
useCases.description: Lets advanced users configure custom sources to automatically resolve IMDB or TMDB IDs into castable video streams.

useCases.title: Format Conversion
useCases.description: Acts as an intermediary to transcode and cast video files or streams that the smart TV natively refuses to play.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Castor is for terminal-savvy users, cord-cutters, and developers who want direct control over casting web media to their local devices. It requires basic familiarity with the command line and optionally FFmpeg for advanced transcoding setups.

changelog.summary: Description changed from "Point it at any web page and it finds the video, extracts the stream, transcodes it and casts in real time to your TV. I" to "Point it at any web page and it finds the video, transcodes it, and streams it to your TV in real time. It even burns in".
